page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg5.8xlarge is a dedicated compute-oriented instance belonging to the High Clock Speed instance family. Built on KVM virtualization using the x86_64 architecture, the system is provisioned with 32 dedicated vCPUs utilizing Intel Xeon 6149 processors clocked at a base speed of 3.1 GHz. Memory capacity totals 128.0 GB, which aligns with a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU distribution, ensuring that multithreaded compute tasks are supported by sufficient operational memory.

The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, nor does it provide hardware accelerators or dedicated GPUs. Systems deployed on this instance rely entirely on remote network-attached block storage for root filesystems and persistent operational volumes. Network performance features a baseline throughput of 6 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned directly to the instance, necessitating standard network gateway or elastic IP allocation for ingress and egress traffic.

From an infrastructure cost perspective, the allocation of dedicated 3.1 GHz high-frequency cores alongside a balanced memory pool delivers solid execution efficiency for CPU-bound tasks without requiring high-density memory overprovisioning. However, reliance on network storage means storage throughput and input/output latency are bounded by network and attached disk limitations. This configuration fits enterprise web serving tiers, automated build and CI/CD pipelines, backend microservices, data processing batch jobs, and compute-focused relational databases.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg5.8xlarge is a high-clock-speed instance engineered for compute-heavy and enterprise application workloads. Configured on the KVM hypervisor with an x86_64 architecture, the instance incorporates 32 dedicated vCPUs powered by Intel Xeon 6149 processors operating at a sustained clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The platform provides 128.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes no local storage or onboard GPU acceleration, requiring external block storage for operating system images and persistent data. Network connectivity is supported by a 6 Gbps baseline bandwidth profile, without bundled complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Given its combination of high CPU frequencies and balanced memory sizing, the instance yields strong processing efficiency relative to lower-frequency virtualized tiers. It is suited for enterprise application serving, batch processing pipelines, continuous integration build nodes, and compute-focused relational database workloads.
